components.note: 鱼 (fish) — fins are a body part belonging to fish.
耆 (qí) gives the sound — an exact match with 鳍's reading.

example.pinyin: Yú yòng qí zài shuǐ lǐ yóuyǒng.
example.english: Fish use fins to swim in water.
example.fact: 鳍 only appears in words about fish anatomy, like 鱼鳍 (yúqí, 'fish fin') — a narrow, technical character outside that context.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 菱 names a water plant.
夌 (líng) gives the sound — an exact match with 菱's reading.

example.pinyin: Māma mǎi le yìxiē língjiao.
example.english: Mom bought some water caltrops.
example.fact: 菱角 (língjiao) is a diamond-shaped water plant whose seed pods are boiled and eaten as a snack in China.

etymologyHint: A small 戋 dish 皿; 戋 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 戋 depicts something small or slight.
皿 (a dish/vessel) — combined with 戋, the image of a small dish gave 盏 its meaning 'small cup' and, by extension, its use as a classifier for lamps and cups.

example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yì zhǎn dēng.
example.english: There is a lamp in the room.
example.fact: 盏 is a classifier used specifically for lamps and cups, as in 一盏灯 (yī zhǎn dēng, 'a lamp').

components.note: 匸 (a box, a hiding place) — 匿 relates to concealment.
若 (ruò) gives a sound distantly related to 匿's reading nì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì fēng nìmíng xìn.
example.english: This is an anonymous letter.
example.fact: 匿 most often appears in 匿名 (nìmíng, 'anonymous'), literally 'to hide one's name.'

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吱 relates to a small sound being made.
支 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match with 吱's reading.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshǔ fāchū zhīzhī de shēngyīn.
example.english: The mouse makes a squeaking sound.
example.fact: 吱 is an onomatopoeia for small squeaking or creaking sounds, like a mouse's cry or a door's hinge — often doubled as 吱吱.

meanings: (bound form) to lie down to sleep or rest
etymologyHint: A person 彐冖又 lying down on a bed 丬 in their home 宀

components.note: 宀 depicts a roof — the character is set inside a home.
丬 represents a bed; combined with a reclining figure under the roof, giving 寝 its meaning 'to sleep, a bed chamber.'

example.pinyin: Wǒmen de qǐnshì hěn gānjìng.
example.english: Our dorm room is very clean.
example.fact: 寝 appears in 寝室 (qǐnshì, 'dormitory room'), a common word for student housing in China.

meanings: to take into one's arms; to embrace

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 揽 relates to grasping or taking hold of something.
览 (lǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 揽's reading.

example.hanzi: 他包揽了比赛的第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā bāolǎn le bǐsài de dì-yī míng.
example.english: He swept first place in the competition.
example.fact: 揽 combines with 包 to form 包揽 (bāolǎn), meaning to take everything on by oneself, like sweeping all the top prizes.

components.note: 骨 (bone) — bone marrow is found inside bones.
遀 (suí) gives a sound close to 髓's reading suǐ, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Gǔsuǐ duì shēntǐ hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Bone marrow is very important to the body.
example.fact: 髓 almost always appears in 骨髓 (gǔsuǐ, 'bone marrow'), including in 骨髓移植 ('bone marrow transplant').

etymologyHint: A hand 彐 grasping a bundle of grain 禾

components.note: 禾 (a grain plant) — the bundle being held.
彐 depicts a hand — a hand grasping a bundle of grain, giving 秉 its meaning 'to grasp, hold.'

example.pinyin: Wǒmen bǐngchéng jiālǐ de chuántǒng.
example.english: We carry on the family's traditions.
example.fact: 秉 rarely stands alone today; it mainly survives in literary compounds like 秉承 (bǐngchéng, 'to follow, carry on') and 秉性 (bǐngxìng, 'inherent nature').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哺 relates to feeding.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 哺's reading bǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Māo shì bǔrǔ dòngwù.
example.english: Cats are mammals.
example.fact: 哺 appears in 哺乳动物 (bǔrǔ dòngwù, 'mammal') — literally 'animal that feeds with milk' — and 哺育 (bǔyù, 'to nurture, raise').

components.note: 矢 is a simple drawing of an arrow, pointed at one end with feathered fletching at the other.

example.pinyin: 'Shǐ' zài gǔdài de yìsi shì jiàn.
example.english: In ancient times, '矢' meant 'arrow.'
example.fact: 矢 is an old literary word for 'arrow' — replaced by 箭 in modern speech — and by extension came to mean 'to vow,' as in 矢志不渝 (shǐzhì bùyú, 'to vow unwaveringly').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啪 relates to a sound being made.
拍 (pāi) gives a sound close to 啪's reading pā, sharing the same initial though the final has shifted slightly.

example.pinyin: Qìqiú pā de yì shēng pò le.
example.english: The balloon popped with a bang.
example.fact: 啪 imitates a sharp snapping or popping sound, like a balloon bursting or a door slamming shut.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — flags and banners are made of cloth.
只 (zhǐ) gives a close sound cue for 帜's reading zhì, sharing the same base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō qízhì.
example.english: There are many flags in the square.
example.fact: 帜 almost always appears in 旗帜 (qízhì, 'flag, banner'), rarely standing alone in modern speech.

components.note: 阝 (a place/settlement) — 邵 relates to a place name.
召 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to 邵's reading shào, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shào shì yí gè xìng.
example.english: Shao is a surname.
example.fact: 邵 is mainly used as a surname and in place names — it doesn't carry an independent meaning in everyday vocabulary.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — coughing is an action of the mouth.
欶 gives a sound distantly related to 嗽's reading sòu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, yìzhí késou.
example.english: I have a cold and keep coughing.
example.fact: 嗽 essentially only appears in 咳嗽 (késou, 'to cough') — it's rarely seen used alone.

meanings: (bound form) to clasp under the arm
etymologyHint: Wedged 夹 in one's arms 扌; 夹 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand/arm) — the part of the body doing the holding.
夹 depicts something squeezed between two sides — combined with the arm, giving 挟 its meaning 'to clasp under the arm.'

example.pinyin: Tā xié zhe yì bǎ sǎn zǒu le.
example.english: He walked off with an umbrella tucked under his arm.
example.fact: 挟's literal meaning is to hold something clasped under the arm; today it's more common in the extended sense 要挟 (yāoxié, 'to coerce') or 挟持 (xiéchí, 'to hold hostage').

components.note: 缶 (an earthenware vessel) — 缸 names a type of pottery container.
工 (gōng) gives a sound related to 缸's reading gāng, though the final has shifted.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yí gè yúgāng.
example.english: My family has a fish tank.
example.fact: 缸 names a wide, deep container, most familiar today in 鱼缸 (yúgāng, 'fish tank') and 水缸 (shuǐgāng, 'water jar').

etymologyHint: A gentle 柔 hand 扌; 柔 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the part of the body doing the rubbing.
柔 (gentle, soft) — a soft, gentle motion of the hand, giving 揉 its meaning 'to rub, massage.'

example.pinyin: Māma róu le róu wǒ de tóu.
example.english: Mom gently rubbed my head.
example.fact: 揉 describes a gentle rubbing or kneading motion, as in 揉眼睛 (róu yǎnjing, 'to rub one's eyes') or kneading dough.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 腻 relates to fattiness.
贰 (èr) gives a sound distantly related to 腻's reading nì, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.pinyin: Zhège cài tài yóunì le.
example.english: This dish is too greasy.
example.fact: 腻 describes food that's greasy or rich (油腻, yóunì), and by extension being sick of something, as in 吃腻了 (chī nì le, 'to be tired of eating something').

components.note: 马 (horse) — 驯 relates to taming animals, especially horses.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to 驯's reading xún, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.pinyin: Rénmen xúnfú le zhè zhī yěmǎ.
example.english: People tamed this wild horse.
example.fact: 驯 describes taming wild animals, as in 驯服 (xúnfú, 'to tame') and 驯养 (xúnyǎng, 'to domesticate') — the horse radical reflects that taming horses was central to its original meaning.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — ropes and cables are made of twisted thread or fiber.
览 (lǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 缆's reading.

example.pinyin: Gōngrén zài xiū diànlǎn.
example.english: Workers are repairing the cable.
example.fact: 缆 names thick ropes or cables, seen today in 电缆 (diànlǎn, 'electric cable') and 缆车 (lǎnchē, 'cable car').

meanings: unit land measurement equal to seven mou (

components.note: 日 (sun) — 晌 relates to a time of day.
向 (xiàng) gives a sound distantly related to 晌's reading shǎng, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.pinyin: Shǎngwu le, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: It's noon, let's go eat.
example.fact: 晌 appears in the colloquial northern Chinese term 晌午 (shǎngwu, 'noon'), an everyday alternative to 中午.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 瘫 names a medical condition.
难 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to 瘫's reading tān, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ tānhuàn le.
example.english: His legs are paralyzed.
example.fact: 瘫痪 (tānhuàn) describes paralysis of the body, and is also used figuratively for systems that stop working entirely, like 交通瘫痪 ('traffic paralysis').

etymologyHint: Money 贝 kept under one 一 roof 宀

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — valuables being kept safe.
宀 (a roof) — valuables kept under a roof, giving 贮 its meaning 'to store, stockpile.'

example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng kěyǐ zhùcún shíwù.
example.english: The fridge can store food.
example.fact: 贮 is a formal word for storing things, most often seen in 贮存 (zhùcún) and 贮藏 (zhùcáng), both meaning 'to store.'

etymologyHint: To search for something with eyes 见 and hands 爫

components.note: 见 (to see) — searching with the eyes.
爫 (a hand) — searching with the hands too, giving 觅 its meaning 'to seek, search.'

example.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo zài mìshí.
example.english: The little bird is searching for food.
example.fact: 觅 is a literary word for 'to seek,' most commonly seen today in 觅食 (mìshí, 'to search for food').

meanings: used in 朦朧|朦胧[meng2 long2]

components.note: 月 (moon) — 朦 describes the moon's hazy appearance.
蒙 (méng) gives the sound — an exact match with 朦's reading.

example.pinyin: Yuèguāng hěn ménglóng.
example.english: The moonlight is hazy and dim.
example.fact: 朦 almost only appears in 朦胧 (ménglóng, 'hazy, dim'), describing blurred light, most often moonlight, or a vague state of mind.

etymologyHint: people living out of the way

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僻 originally described people living out of the way.
辟 (pì) gives the sound — an exact match with 僻's reading.

example.hanzi: 他住在一个偏僻的小村子。
example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yí gè piānpì de xiǎo cūnzi.
example.english: He lives in a remote little village.
example.fact: 僻 combines with 偏 to form 偏僻 (piānpì, 'remote, out-of-the-way'), and also appears in 怪僻 (guàipì, 'eccentric').

example.hanzi: 隋朝是中国历史上的一个朝代。
example.pinyin: Suí Cháo shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng de yí gè cháodài.
example.english: The Sui dynasty was a dynasty in Chinese history.
example.fact: 隋 names the Sui dynasty (581–617 AD), a short-lived dynasty that reunified China before the Tang dynasty followed it.

meanings: (bound form) trailing or climbing stem; vine
etymologyHint: A long 曼 plant 艹 ; 曼 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing that is growing.
曼 (long, extended) — a plant that stretches out long and trailing, giving 蔓 its meaning 'vine, tendril.'

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng zhǎngmǎn le téngmàn.
example.english: The wall is covered with vines.
example.fact: 蔓 names the long, trailing stems of climbing plants (藤蔓, téngmàn), and by extension 蔓延 (mànyán) means 'to spread' — like a vine creeping outward.

meanings: dialectal equivalent of 怎麼|怎么[zen3 me5]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咋 is a spoken question particle.
乍 (zhà) gives a sound distantly related to 咋's reading zǎ, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè kě zǎ bàn ne?
example.english: What should we do about this?
example.fact: 咋 is a colloquial northern Chinese word meaning 'how, why,' as in 咋办 (zǎbàn, 'what to do') — a dialect equivalent of 怎么.

meanings: see 赤嵌樓|赤嵌楼[Chi4 kan3 lou2]

components.note: 山 (mountain) — the shape radical here; its literal meaning doesn't map directly onto 嵌's sense of 'inlay,' a common pattern for characters whose imagery has faded.
欠 (qiàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 嵌's reading.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng qiàn zhe yí kuài yùshí.
example.english: A piece of jade is embedded in the wall.
example.fact: 嵌 means to fit or embed one thing into another, as in 镶嵌 (xiāngqiàn, 'to inlay') — think of a jewel set into a ring.

example.pinyin: Tā qiánchéng de qídǎo.
example.english: He prayed devoutly.
example.fact: 虔 almost always appears in 虔诚 (qiánchéng, 'devout, pious'), describing sincere religious reverence.

etymologyHint: A farm 田 divided in half 半; 半 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 田 (a field) — the land whose edge is being described.
半 (half) — a field divided along a boundary line, giving 畔 its meaning 'bank, edge, side.'

example.pinyin: Tāmen zài húpàn sànbù.
example.english: They took a walk by the lake.
example.fact: 畔 is a literary word for 'bank, edge,' most often seen in 湖畔 (húpàn, 'lakeside') and 河畔 (hépàn, 'riverside').

components.note: 王 (jade) — 琐 originally referred to small, ornamental pieces of jade, extended to 'trifling.'
⺌ is the historical phonetic element in 琐's traditional form 瑣; its sound value has become opaque in the modern simplified character.

example.pinyin: Shēnghuó zhōng yǒu hěn duō suǒshì.
example.english: There are many trivial matters in daily life.
example.fact: 琐 describes small, trivial things, as in 琐事 (suǒshì, 'trivial matters') and 琐碎 (suǒsuì, 'petty, fragmented').

etymologyHint: A flat 枼 stone 石

components.note: 石 (stone) — early dishes were sometimes made of or associated with stone/ceramic material.
枼 depicts something flat and thin, giving 碟 its meaning 'a small, flat dish.'

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí gè diézi.
example.english: There is a small plate on the table.
example.fact: 碟 names a small, flat dish (碟子, diézi), and by shape extension also means 'disc,' as in 光碟 (guāngdié, 'CD, disc').

etymologyHint: Water 氵 that cuts like a knife 刃; 止 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 氵 (water) — a liquid quality being described.
刃 (a blade) — something that feels sharp or rough going down, giving 涩 its meaning 'astringent, harsh.'

example.pinyin: Zhège shìzi hái hěn sè.
example.english: This persimmon is still very astringent.
example.fact: 涩 describes an astringent, puckering taste, like an unripe persimmon, and by extension 羞涩 (xiūsè) describes someone being shy or bashful.

meanings: used in 朦朧|朦胧[meng2 long2]

components.note: 月 (moon) — 胧 describes the moon's hazy appearance.
龙 (lóng) gives the sound — an exact match with 胧's reading.

example.pinyin: Yuǎnchù de yuèsè ménglóng.
example.english: The moonlight in the distance is hazy.
example.fact: 胧 exists only in the compound 朦胧 (ménglóng, 'hazy, dim'), almost never appearing alone.

meanings: (onom.) toot; honk; beep (sound of a horn etc)

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘟 relates to a sound or shape made with the mouth.
都 (dū) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘟's reading.

example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi dū zhe zuǐ bù gāoxìng.
example.english: The child pouted, unhappy.
example.fact: 嘟 imitates a honking or tooting sound, like a car horn, and in 嘟嘴 (dūzuǐ) describes pouting, pushing the lips out.

meanings: to jump; to bounce; to hop

components.note: 足 (foot) — 蹦 relates to an action done with the legs and feet.
崩 (bēng) gives a sound close to 蹦's reading bèng, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Háizimen gāoxìng de bèngtiào zhe.
example.english: The children happily jumped around.
example.fact: 蹦 describes hopping or bouncing, often in 蹦跳 (bèngtiào) and the loanword 蹦极 (bèngjí, 'bungee jumping').

meanings: senior (i.e. eldest child or senior in rank)

components.note: 冖 (a cover) — a mound covering a grave.
豖 gives a sound distantly related to 冢's reading zhǒng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shān shàng yǒu yí zuò gǔzhǒng.
example.english: There is an ancient burial mound on the mountain.
example.fact: 冢 is a literary word for a burial mound or grave, most often seen today in historical or literary contexts like 古冢 (gǔzhǒng, 'ancient tomb').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浏 originally described clear, bright water.
刘 (liú) gives the sound — an exact match with 浏's reading.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan liúlǎn wǎngyè.
example.english: I like browsing web pages.
example.fact: 浏 mainly survives in 浏览 (liúlǎn, 'to browse, skim'), a word used constantly for reading webpages or skimming books.

components.note: 冏 depicts brightness, an open window; its link to 裔's meaning 'descendants' has faded over time, a common pattern in characters whose original imagery no longer maps clearly onto the current meaning.
衣 (yī) gives a sound close to 裔's reading yì, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā shì nà wèi huángdì de hòuyì.
example.english: He is a descendant of that emperor.
example.fact: 裔 almost always appears in 后裔 (hòuyì, 'descendant'), a formal word for someone descended from a notable ancestor.

etymologyHint: Cloth 衤 that restricts 禁; 禁 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 襟 relates to a part of a garment.
禁 (to restrict) — cloth that closes and restrains the garment, giving 襟 its meaning 'lapel, front flap.'

example.pinyin: Tā de yījīn bèi fēng chuī kāi le.
example.english: His lapel was blown open by the wind.
example.fact: 襟 names the front flap or lapel of traditional Chinese clothing (衣襟, yījīn), where the fabric overlaps and is fastened.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 叨 relates to talking.
刀 (dāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 叨's reading.

example.pinyin: Māma zǒngshì láodao wǒ.
example.english: Mom always nags me.
example.fact: 叨 appears in 唠叨 (láodao, 'to nag, be talkative'), describing someone who repeats themselves endlessly.

etymologyHint: Words 讠 said at a parting 夬; 夬 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诀 relates to words that are said.
夬 depicts a decisive break or parting — words said at a final parting, giving 诀 its meaning 'to bid farewell' and 'a secret trick.'

example.pinyin: Chénggōng de mìjué shì nǔlì.
example.english: The secret to success is hard work.
example.fact: 诀 appears in 秘诀 (mìjué, 'secret trick, knack'), a common word for the key behind success, and in 诀别 (juébié, 'to part forever').

components.note: 日 (sun) — 旭 describes the sun at dawn.
九 (jiǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 旭's reading xù, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.pinyin: Xùrì cóng dōngfāng shēngqǐ.
example.english: The rising sun comes up in the east.
example.fact: 旭 specifically describes the sun rising, as in the set phrase 旭日东升 (xùrì dōngshēng, 'the rising sun ascends in the east'), a symbol of a bright new beginning.

meanings: used in 蝦蟆|虾蟆[ha2 ma5]

components.note: 虫 (insect/small creature) — 虾 names a small water creature.
下 (xià) gives a sound close to 虾's reading xiā, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī xiā.
example.english: I like eating shrimp.
example.fact: 虾 uses the 虫 (bug) radical because in traditional categorization, small creatures like shrimp were grouped with insects.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early records were written on bamboo strips.
溥 (pǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 簿's reading bù, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zài bùzi shàng xiě zì.
example.english: He writes in the notebook.
example.fact: 簿 names a notebook or register, as in 簿子 (bùzi, 'notebook') and 账簿 (zhàngbù, 'account book') — its bamboo radical reflects that early Chinese records were written on bamboo strips.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啤 relates to a drink.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound related to 啤's reading pí, though the consonant and vowel have both shifted somewhat.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan hē píjiǔ.
example.english: He likes drinking beer.
example.fact: 啤 exists solely to write 啤酒 (píjiǔ, 'beer'), a phonetic loanword created for the English word 'beer.'

etymologyHint: To catch 禽 by hand 扌; 禽 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the act of catching is done by hand.
禽 (a bird, game animal) — catching an animal by hand, giving 擒 its meaning 'to catch, capture.'

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá qínhuò le xiǎotōu.
example.english: The police captured the thief.
example.fact: 擒 means 'to catch, capture,' as in 擒获 (qínhuò) and the idiom 欲擒故纵 (yù qín gù zòng, 'to loosen the leash in order to catch').

etymologyHint: Dates ⺀ falling off a tree 朿

components.note: 朿 depicts a thorny tree — jujube trees have thorny branches.
⺀ (dots) — dates falling from the thorny tree, giving 枣 its meaning 'date, jujube.'

example.pinyin: Nǎinai xǐhuan chī zǎo.
example.english: Grandma likes eating dates.
example.fact: 枣 refers to the jujube (Chinese date), a fruit widely eaten fresh or dried, and often added to tea or soup in Chinese cooking.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘎 relates to a sound being made.
戛 (jiá) gives a sound distantly related to 嘎's reading gā, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Yāzi gāgā de jiào.
example.english: The duck quacks 'ga ga.'
example.fact: 嘎 is an onomatopoeia for sharp, creaking sounds — most familiarly a duck's quack (嘎嘎, gāgā).

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苑 names a garden or park full of plants.
夗 gives the sound — an exact match with 苑's reading yuàn.

example.pinyin: Gǔdài de huāyuàn shífēn měilì.
example.english: The ancient garden was very beautiful.
example.fact: 苑 is a literary word for 'garden, park,' historically describing royal grounds where animals and plants were kept — today mostly seen in place names and formal writing.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 牟 originally described the sound an ox makes.

example.pinyin: Tā zuò shēngyì shì wèile móulì.
example.english: He does business in order to make profit.
example.fact: 牟 originally imitated the sound of an ox mooing; today it survives mainly in 牟利 (móulì, 'to seek profit'), often with a negative connotation of profiteering.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — vomiting happens through the mouth.
区 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 呕's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他生病了，呕吐了好几次。
example.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng le, ǒutù le hǎo jǐ cì.
example.english: He got sick and vomited several times.
example.fact: 呕 appears in 呕吐 (ǒutù, 'to vomit') and the idiom 呕心沥血 (ǒuxīn lìxuè, 'to pour out one's heart and blood'), describing painstaking effort.

meanings: a white horse with black mane
white horse with a black mane (archaic)

components.note: 马 (horse) — 骆 originally described a kind of horse, later extended to camels.
各 (gè) gives a sound distantly related to 骆's reading luò, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shāmò lǐ yǒu hěn duō luòtuo.
example.english: There are many camels in the desert.
example.fact: 骆 exists almost only in 骆驼 (luòtuo, 'camel'), the animal famous for crossing deserts.

components.note: 凸 is a line drawing of a shape bulging outward from a flat rectangle — a visual pictogram for 'convex, protruding.'

example.pinyin: Tā de dùzi yǒudiǎn tū chūlái.
example.english: His belly sticks out a bit.
example.fact: 凸 is a rare case of a purely visual character — its shape literally draws a bump sticking out of a flat line, giving it the meaning 'convex, protruding.'

etymologyHint: To end 息 a flame 火; 息 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 火 (fire) — the flame that is put out.
息 (to stop, rest) — bringing a flame to a stop, giving 熄 its meaning 'to extinguish.'

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ huǒ xīmiè le.
example.english: He put out the fire.
example.fact: 熄 means to extinguish a flame or light, as in 熄灭 (xīmiè) and 熄火 (xīhuǒ, 'to turn off an engine,' literally 'extinguish the fire').

etymologyHint: Cutting 一 off the feet 儿

components.note: 儿 depicts a person's legs.
一, shown across the legs, pictures cutting off the feet — an ancient punishment — giving 兀 its literary sense of being cut short or standing bare.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān kàn qǐlái hěn tūwù.
example.english: This mountain looks abruptly towering.
example.fact: 兀 is rare alone today, mostly surviving in 突兀 (tūwù, 'abrupt, jarring' or 'towering'), describing something that rises or appears suddenly.

meanings: descriptive of crying or of crowing

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 喔 relates to a sound being made.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to 喔's reading ō, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gōngjī ō ō de jiào.
example.english: The rooster crows 'o-o.'
example.fact: 喔 imitates a rooster's crow, usually doubled as 喔喔 (ō ō) — the Chinese equivalent of English 'cock-a-doodle-doo.'

components.note: 衣 (clothes) — 裳 names an article of clothing.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound close to 裳's reading, matching the base syllable exactly in this neutral-tone usage.

example.pinyin: Māma mǎi le xīn yīshang.
example.english: Mom bought new clothes.
example.fact: 裳 combines with 衣 to form the colloquial word 衣裳 (yīshang, 'clothes'), where 裳 is pronounced in the neutral tone 'shang.'

components.note: 凹 is a line drawing of a shape dented inward from a flat rectangle — a visual pictogram for 'concave, hollow.'

example.hanzi: 路上有一个凹陷的地方。
example.pinyin: Lù shàng yǒu yí gè āoxiàn de dìfang.
example.english: There's a hollow in the road.
example.fact: 凹 is 凸's mirror image — instead of bulging out, its shape dents inward, giving it the meaning 'concave, hollow.'

etymologyHint: To sell 卖 a soul for money 贝; 卖 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — the payment involved.
卖 (to sell) — combined with money, the image of buying something back, giving 赎 its meaning 'to redeem, ransom.'

example.pinyin: Tāmen fù le shújīn.
example.english: They paid the ransom.
example.fact: 赎 means 'to redeem, buy back,' as in 赎金 (shújīn, 'ransom money') and 赎罪 (shúzuì, 'to atone for a sin').

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè xiǎo túnzi.
example.english: This is a small village.
example.fact: 屯 names a small village or hamlet, common in northern Chinese place names, and as a verb means 'to station troops' or 'to hoard' (屯兵, 屯粮).

etymologyHint: A hall 堂 in one's chest ⺼; 堂 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — the chest is part of the body.
堂 (a hall) — a hall-like hollow space inside the chest, giving 膛 its meaning 'chest cavity.'

example.pinyin: Tā tǐng qǐ xiōngtáng.
example.english: He puffed out his chest.
example.fact: 膛 names the hollow cavity of the chest (胸膛, xiōngtáng), and by extension the bore of a gun barrel (枪膛, qiāngtáng).

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浇 relates to pouring water.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound distantly related to 浇's reading jiāo, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gěi huā jiāoshuǐ.
example.english: I water the flowers every day.
example.fact: 浇 means 'to pour water on,' most commonly in 浇水 (jiāoshuǐ, 'to water plants').

meanings: to burn; to sear; to scorch

components.note: 火 (fire) — 灼 relates to burning.
勺 (sháo) gives a sound distantly related to 灼's reading zhuó, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shāmò de tàiyáng hěn zhuórè.
example.english: The desert sun is scorching hot.
example.fact: 灼 means 'to burn, scorch,' most often seen in 灼热 (zhuórè, 'scorching hot').

components.note: 衣 (clothes) — 裘 names a type of garment.
求 (qiú) gives the sound — an exact match with 裘's reading.

example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tā chuān zhe píqiú.
example.english: In winter he wears a fur coat.
example.fact: 裘 is a literary word for a fur coat, largely replaced today by 皮衣 (píyī) in everyday speech, and also used as a surname.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 砰 relates to an impact, as of something crashing.
平 (píng) gives a sound related to 砰's reading pēng, sharing the initial though the final has shifted.

example.pinyin: Mén pēng de yì shēng guān shàng le.
example.english: The door slammed shut with a bang.
example.fact: 砰 imitates a loud crashing or banging sound, often a door slamming shut.

components.note: 朿 (a thorny branch) — 棘 doubles this shape to depict a thorny bramble.
朿 is repeated here rather than serving as a separate phonetic borrowing — the character's reading jí comes from the doubled thorn form itself.

example.pinyin: Lù shàng zhǎngmǎn le jīngjí.
example.english: The road is overgrown with thorny brambles.
example.fact: 棘 pictures two thorn branches stacked together, vividly showing a thorny bramble; it appears today in 荆棘 (jīngjí, 'thorns, brambles').

components.note: 木 (tree) — 橡 names a type of tree.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 橡's reading.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xiàngpí bújiàn le.
example.english: My eraser is missing.
example.fact: 橡 names rubber and the rubber tree, most familiar in 橡皮 (xiàngpí, 'eraser,' literally 'rubber skin') and 橡胶 (xiàngjiāo, 'rubber').

components.note: 石 (mineral/stone) — 碱 names a mineral substance.
咸 (xián) gives a sound distantly related to 碱's reading jiǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Féizào lǐ hányǒu jiǎn.
example.english: Soap contains alkali.
example.fact: 碱 is the chemistry term for 'alkali, base' — the opposite of acid (酸) — commonly seen in 碱性 (jiǎnxìng, 'alkaline').

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 聋 describes a condition of the ear.
龙 (lóng) gives the sound — an exact match with 聋's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā ěrduo lóng le, tīng bu jiàn.
example.english: His ears are deaf; he can't hear.
example.fact: 聋 means 'deaf,' as in 耳聋 (ěrlóng) and 聋哑人 (lóngyǎrén, 'deaf-mute person').

etymologyHint: An older 老 woman 女; 老 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 女 (woman) — 姥 names a female relative.
老 (old) — an older woman, giving 姥 its meaning 'grandmother.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ lǎolao jīnnián qīshí suì le.
example.english: My maternal grandma is seventy this year.
example.fact: 姥 appears in 姥姥 (lǎolao, 'maternal grandmother'), the common colloquial term used in northern Mandarin, alongside 外婆 in the south.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 瑜 originally described a flawless jade gem.
俞 (yú) gives the sound — an exact match with 瑜's reading.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān liànxí yújiā.
example.english: I practice yoga every day.
example.fact: 瑜 originally meant the luster of fine jade; today it's most often seen in 瑜伽 (yújiā, 'yoga'), a phonetic borrowing unrelated to the original meaning.

example.hanzi: 古文里，'毋' 的意思是'不要'。
example.pinyin: Gǔwén lǐ, 'wú' de yìsi shì 'búyào'.
example.english: In classical Chinese, '毋' means 'don't.'
example.fact: 毋 is a classical Chinese negative, roughly equivalent to modern 不 or 不要; today it survives mainly in set phrases like 毋庸置疑 (wúyōng zhìyí, 'undoubtedly').

meanings: mutual term of address used by sons-in-law

components.note: 女 (woman) — 娅 names a female relation or is used in women's names.
亚 (yà) gives the sound — an exact match with 娅's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā de míngzi jiào Ānyà.
example.english: Her name is Anya.
example.fact: 娅 is used mainly to transliterate foreign women's names, like 安娅 (Ānyà, 'Anya'), rather than carrying an independent meaning in modern speech.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the radical here, though 沮's meaning has shifted well away from water.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to 沮's reading jǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Kǎoshì méi kǎo hǎo, tā hěn jǔsàng.
example.english: He did poorly on the exam and felt dejected.
example.fact: 沮 mainly appears in 沮丧 (jǔsàng, 'dejected, disheartened'), describing a low, discouraged mood.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 萌 describes a plant sprouting.
明 (míng) gives a sound close to 萌's reading méng, sharing the initial though the final has shifted slightly.

example.pinyin: Chūntiān, xiǎo cǎo kāishǐ méngyá.
example.english: In spring, the grass starts to sprout.
example.fact: 萌 originally meant a plant's bud sprouting (萌芽, méngyá); in contemporary slang, it's also borrowed to mean 'cute, adorable,' from the Japanese moe.

etymologyHint: A similar 肖 person 亻; 肖 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — 俏 describes a person's look.
肖 (to resemble) — someone resembling an attractive ideal, giving 俏 its meaning 'pretty, charming.'

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn qiàopí.
example.english: She looks cute and lively.
example.fact: 俏 describes someone pretty, lively, or charming, as in 俏皮 (qiàopí, 'cute, witty') and 俊俏 (jùnqiào, 'good-looking').

components.note: 黑 (black) — 黯 relates to darkness.
音 (yīn) gives a sound distantly related to 黯's reading àn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tiānsè biàn de àndàn.
example.english: The sky turned dim and dark.
example.fact: 黯 describes deep darkness or gloom, as in 黯淡 (àndàn, 'dim, gloomy') and 黯然 (ànrán, 'dejected, downcast').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撇 relates to an action done by hand, tossing something aside.
敝 (bì) gives a sound distantly related to 撇's reading piē, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān piēkāi zhège wèntí.
example.english: Let's set this problem aside for now.
example.fact: 撇 means 'to cast aside,' as in 撇开 (piēkāi, 'to set aside') — the same character, read piě, also names the left-falling 丿 stroke in Chinese calligraphy.

etymologyHint: A millet plant 米 bearing grain 覀

components.note: 米 (rice/grain) — the grain being pictured.
覀 depicts a stylized head of grain atop a plant, giving 粟 its meaning 'millet.'

example.pinyin: Gǔdài rén chī sù mǐ.
example.english: Ancient people ate millet.
example.fact: 粟 names millet, a staple grain in ancient China before rice became dominant; today it mostly survives in the idiom 沧海一粟 (cānghǎi yī sù, 'a grain in the vast sea,' meaning something insignificant).

components.note: 米 (grain) — the character's upper part traces back to imagery of separating grain-like matter.
共 (gòng) gives a sound distantly related to 粪's reading fèn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 农民用粪便给庄稼施肥。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín yòng fènbiàn gěi zhuāngjia shīféi.
example.english: Farmers use manure to fertilize crops.
example.fact: 粪 means 'excrement, manure,' as in 粪便 (fènbiàn) — a common and useful agricultural term for fertilizer despite its unglamorous meaning.

components.note: 尹 is an old pictograph of a hand holding a scepter or staff of office, symbolizing authority.

example.pinyin: Yǐn shì yí gè Zhōngguó xìngshì.
example.english: Yin is a Chinese surname.
example.fact: 尹 originally pictured a hand gripping a staff of authority; today it's mainly seen as a surname and in the ancient official title 令尹 (lìngyǐn, a chief minister of the state of Chu).

components.note: 艹 (wild grass) — 苟 relates to something lowly or careless, like wild, untended grass.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to 苟's reading gǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zuòshì yìsī bùgǒu.
example.english: He does things meticulously.
example.fact: 苟 originally meant 'careless, frivolous'; today it's best known in the idiom 一丝不苟 (yīsī bùgǒu, 'not the least bit careless,' i.e. meticulous).

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 癫 names a mental or neurological condition.
颠 (diān) gives the sound — an exact match with 癫's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái yǒudiǎn fēngdiān.
example.english: He looks a little crazy.
example.fact: 癫 describes madness or crazed behavior, as in 疯癫 (fēngdiān, 'crazy, deranged') and 癫痫 (diānxián, 'epilepsy').

meanings: used in 螞螂|蚂螂[ma1 lang2]
used in 螞蟥|蚂蟥[ma3 huang2]
used in 螞蟻|蚂蚁[ma3 yi3]
used in 螞蚱|蚂蚱[ma4 zha5]

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蚂 names a small crawling creature.
马 (mǎ) gives the sound — an exact match with 蚂's reading.

example.pinyin: Dìshang yǒu hěn duō mǎyǐ.
example.english: There are many ants on the ground.
example.fact: 蚂 exists almost only in 蚂蚁 (mǎyǐ, 'ant') and 蚂蚱 (màzha, 'grasshopper').

example.hanzi: 大禹是中国传说中的英雄。
example.pinyin: Dàyǔ shì Zhōngguó chuánshuō zhōng de yīngxióng.
example.english: Yu the Great is a legendary hero in China.
example.fact: 禹 names a legendary ancient ruler credited with controlling a great flood and founding the Xia dynasty — one of the most celebrated figures in early Chinese history and mythology.

etymologyHint: The wind 翏 blowing over a vast, empty plain 广

components.note: 广 depicts a wide, sheltering structure — a vast, open space.
翏 evokes wind and feathers in flight, sweeping across that open expanse.

example.pinyin: Liào shì yí gè chángjiàn de xìng.
example.english: Liao is a common surname.
example.fact: 廖 today is used almost exclusively as a Chinese surname; it no longer carries an independent meaning in daily vocabulary.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 俭 describes a personal trait.
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 俭's reading jiǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Nǎinai shēnghuó hěn jiéjiǎn.
example.english: Grandma lives very frugally.
example.fact: 俭 means 'frugal, thrifty,' as in 节俭 (jiéjiǎn) — a virtue traditionally praised in Chinese culture.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — writing was once done on cloth.
占 (to mark, occupy) — marking something down on cloth, giving 帖 its meaning 'a note, card.'

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shìqing bàn de hěn tuǒtiē.
example.english: He handled the matter very properly and smoothly.
example.fact: When read tiē, 帖 means 'fitting, in good order,' as in 妥帖 (tuǒtiē, 'appropriate, well-arranged') — a different reading and meaning from the more common tiě, as in 请帖 (qǐngtiě, 'invitation card').

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 煎 relates to cooking with heat.
前 (qián) gives a sound distantly related to 煎's reading jiān, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Māma zài jiān jīdàn.
example.english: Mom is frying eggs.
example.fact: 煎 means 'to pan-fry,' a common cooking method in Chinese cuisine, as in 煎鸡蛋 (jiān jīdàn, 'fried eggs') and 煎饺 (jiānjiǎo, 'pan-fried dumplings').

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缕 relates to a thin strand.
娄 (lóu) gives a sound related to 缕's reading lǚ, though the final has shifted.

example.pinyin: Yì lǚ yángguāng zhào jìn fángjiān.
example.english: A ray of sunlight shines into the room.
example.fact: 缕 is a measure word for thin strands or wisps, as in 一缕阳光 (yī lǚ yángguāng, 'a ray of sunlight') and 一缕头发 (yī lǚ tóufa, 'a strand of hair').

etymologyHint: To buy someone off 卖; a nose-hole 穴

components.note: 穴 (a hole/cavity) — 窦 names an opening or orifice.
卖 appears here only as a simplified handwriting substitute for the traditional character's shape; it isn't meaningfully related to 卖's sense 'to sell.'

example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de bídòu.
example.english: The doctor examined his sinuses.
example.fact: 窦 names a hole or cavity, most familiar today in the medical term 鼻窦 (bídòu, 'sinus'); it's also a Chinese surname.

meanings: (bound form) to cluster; to pile up
classifier for bunches, clusters, piles etc

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo naturally grows in dense clusters.
族 (zú) gives a sound distantly related to 簇's reading cù, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu yí cù xiānhuā.
example.english: There's a cluster of fresh flowers in the garden.
example.fact: 簇 is a measure word and verb for things clustered together, as in 一簇花 (yī cù huā, 'a cluster of flowers').

meanings: used in 花不棱登[hua1 bu5 leng1 deng1]
used in 撲棱|扑棱[pu1 leng1]

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棱 originally described the edge of a squared timber.
夌 (líng) gives a sound close to 棱's reading léng, sharing the initial and tone and differing only in the vowel.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi de léngjiǎo hěn jiān.
example.english: The table's edges are very sharp.
example.fact: 棱 names the sharp edge or corner of an object, as in 棱角 (léngjiǎo), also used figuratively for someone's sharp, distinct personality.

components.note: 卩 (a kneeling figure) — 叩 relates to kneeling in a bow.
口 (kǒu) gives a sound close to 叩's reading kòu, sharing the initial and final and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā kòu le kòu mén.
example.english: He knocked on the door.
example.fact: 叩 means 'to knock' or, in 叩头/叩拜 (kòutóu/kòubài), 'to kowtow' — bowing with the forehead touching the ground as a sign of deep respect.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 呐 relates to shouting.
内 (nèi) gives a sound related to 呐's reading nà, sharing the initial though the final has shifted.

example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen dàshēng nàhǎn.
example.english: The soldiers shouted loudly.
example.fact: 呐 appears in 呐喊 (nàhǎn, 'to shout, cry out'), a word for a loud rallying cry, famously also the title of a short story collection by the writer Lu Xun.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 瑶 originally described precious jade.
䍃 (yáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 瑶's reading.

example.hanzi: 瑶族是中国的一个少数民族。
example.pinyin: Yáozú shì Zhōngguó de yí gè shǎoshù mínzú.
example.english: The Yao people are an ethnic minority in China.
example.fact: 瑶 originally meant a precious kind of jade; today it's also the name of the Yao ethnic group (瑶族, Yáozú), one of China's 55 recognized minorities.

components.note: 野 (open countryside) — 墅 names a house set in the countryside.
土 (tǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 墅's reading shù, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tāmen jiā yǒu yí zuò biéshù.
example.english: Their family has a villa.
example.fact: 墅 exists almost only in 别墅 (biéshù, 'villa'), a word for a private, often countryside house.

etymologyHint: A bird 鸟 covered in 冖 green 艹 feathers

components.note: 艹 (grass, suggesting green) — hints at the bird's greenish plumage.
鸟 (bird) — 莺 names a small songbird covered in colorful feathers.

example.hanzi: 公园里有一只黄莺在唱歌。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī huángyīng zài chànggē.
example.english: There's an oriole singing in the park.
example.fact: 莺 names small songbirds like the oriole and warbler, as in 黄莺 (huángyīng, 'oriole') — a bird often associated with pleasant song in Chinese poetry.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烫 relates to intense heat.
汤 (tāng) gives a sound close to 烫's reading tàng, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, shuǐ hěn tàng!
example.english: Be careful, the water is very hot!
example.fact: 烫 describes something scalding hot, as in 烫伤 (tàngshāng, 'a scald') — it's also used for 'to perm' hair (烫头发), since perming once involved heat.

components.note: 虫 (small creature) — 蛙 names a small animal, grouped here alongside insects.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to 蛙's reading wā, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō qīngwā.
example.english: There are many frogs in the pond.
example.fact: 蛙 means 'frog,' most commonly in 青蛙 (qīngwā, 'frog') — grouped under the 虫 radical, which traditionally covered small creatures broadly, not just insects.

components.note: 歹 is an old pictograph of a fragment of bone, giving it an association with death, decay, and by extension 'evil, vicious.'

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè dǎitú.
example.english: He is a villain.
example.fact: 歹 means 'bad, vicious,' as in 歹徒 (dǎitú, 'villain, gangster') — it's also Kangxi radical 78, appearing in characters related to death and misfortune, like 死 (sǐ, 'to die').

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伶 describes a kind of person.
令 (lìng) gives a sound close to 伶's reading líng, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn cōngming línglì.
example.english: This child is very clever and quick-witted.
example.fact: 伶 appears in 伶俐 (línglì, 'clever, nimble') and historically named performers or actors (伶人, língrén), an old word for entertainers.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 葱 names a type of vegetable plant.
怱 (cōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 葱's reading.

example.pinyin: Māma qiē le yìxiē cōng.
example.english: Mom chopped some scallions.
example.fact: 葱 names green onions/scallions, a staple aromatic in Chinese cooking, and also describes a fresh green color (葱绿, cōnglǜ).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哮 relates to breathing sounds made through the mouth.
孝 (xiào) gives a sound close to 哮's reading xiāo, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu xiàochuǎn, hūxī kùnnan.
example.english: He has asthma and has trouble breathing.
example.fact: 哮 mainly appears in 哮喘 (xiàochuǎn, 'asthma'), a respiratory condition causing wheezing and difficulty breathing.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眩 relates to dizziness affecting one's vision.
玄 (xuán) gives a sound close to 眩's reading xuàn, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā juéde tóuyūn mùxuàn.
example.english: He felt dizzy and disoriented.
example.fact: 眩 describes dizziness or dazzlement, most often in the set phrase 头晕目眩 (tóuyūn mùxuàn, 'dizzy and seeing stars').

components.note: 申 here ties to 坤's traditional role naming the earth trigram in the Book of Changes, rather than mapping to an everyday literal image.
土 (tǔ) gives a sound distantly related to 坤's reading kūn, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.pinyin: 'Qiánkūn' de yìsi shì tiāndì.
example.english: "Qiánkūn" means heaven and earth.
example.fact: 坤 represents 'earth' and the feminine principle in the Yijing (Book of Changes), often paired with 乾 (qián, 'heaven, masculine') in the word 乾坤 (qiánkūn, 'the universe, everything under heaven').

components.note: 广 (a wide shelter) — 廓 relates to something broad or spacious.
郭 (guō) gives a sound related to 廓's reading kuò, though the initial and vowel have drifted apart somewhat.

example.pinyin: Wǒ néng kàndào shān de lúnkuò.
example.english: I can see the outline of the mountain.
example.fact: 廓 mainly appears in 轮廓 (lúnkuò, 'outline, contour') and 廓清 (kuòqīng, 'to clarify').

meanings: name of deceased emperor or superior

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讳 relates to things not spoken about.
韦 (wéi) gives a sound distantly related to 讳's reading huì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 在中国文化里，有些数字是忌讳的。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó wénhuà lǐ, yǒuxiē shùzì shì jìhuì de.
example.english: In Chinese culture, some numbers are taboo.
example.fact: 讳 mainly appears in 忌讳 (jìhuì, 'taboo, to avoid as inappropriate') and 直言不讳 (zhíyán bùhuì, 'to speak frankly without holding back').

meanings: (bound form) to cry; to weep loudly

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啼 relates to a sound made with the mouth, crying.
帝 (dì) gives a sound related to 啼's reading tí, though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Yīng'ér yìzhí zài tíkū.
example.english: The baby keeps crying.
example.fact: 啼 describes crying or wailing, as in 啼哭 (tíkū), and is also used for animal cries, such as a rooster's crow or a cuckoo's call in classical poetry.

example.hanzi: 乍一看，这个问题很简单。
example.pinyin: Zhà yí kàn, zhège wèntí hěn jiǎndān.
example.english: At first glance, this problem seems simple.
example.fact: 乍 means 'suddenly, for the first time,' most often in 乍一看 (zhà yī kàn, 'at first glance') and 乍看 (zhàkàn).

components.note: 瓜 (melon) — 瓣 relates to how fruit divides into natural segments.
辡 (biàn) gives a sound related to 瓣's reading bàn, sharing the initial and tone though the vowel has shifted.

example.pinyin: Zhè duǒ huā yǒu wǔ piàn huābàn.
example.english: This flower has five petals.
example.fact: 瓣 names a segment or petal, as in 花瓣 (huābàn, 'flower petal') and 蒜瓣 (suànbàn, 'garlic clove') — the melon radical reflects how fruit naturally divides into segments.

meanings: used in 矯情|矫情[jiao2 qing5]

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — 矫 originally described straightening a bent arrow shaft.
乔 (qiáo) gives a sound related to 矫's reading jiǎo, though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 他去牙医那里矫正牙齿。
example.pinyin: Tā qù yáyī nàlǐ jiǎozhèng yáchǐ.
example.english: He went to the dentist to get his teeth straightened.
example.fact: 矫 means 'to correct, straighten,' as in 矫正 (jiǎozhèng) — often used for orthodontic braces (矫正牙齿) or correcting posture.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跋 relates to traveling on foot.
犮 (bá) gives the sound — an exact match with 跋's reading.

example.hanzi: 他们长途跋涉，终于到达了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen chángtú báshè, zhōngyú dàodá le.
example.english: They traveled a long, arduous journey and finally arrived.
example.fact: 跋 appears in 跋涉 (báshè, 'to trek, travel with difficulty') and, separately, names a postscript or afterword at the end of a book.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枉 originally described a bent piece of wood.
王 (wáng) gives a sound close to 枉's reading wǎng, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 你冤枉了他，他是无辜的。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yuānwang le tā, tā shì wúgū de.
example.english: You wronged him unjustly; he is innocent.
example.fact: 枉 means 'in vain' or 'unjustly bent,' as in 冤枉 (yuānwang, 'to wrongly accuse') and 枉费 (wǎngfèi, 'to waste, in vain').

components.note: 木 (tree/plant) — 梗 originally named a plant's stem or branch.
更 (gèng) gives a sound close to 梗's reading gěng, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这是一个很有名的网络梗。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hěn yǒumíng de wǎngluò gěng.
example.english: This is a very famous internet meme.
example.fact: 梗 originally meant a plant's stem or stalk; in contemporary internet slang, it's borrowed to mean 'meme' or 'running joke' (网络梗, wǎngluò gěng).

meanings: (literary) to be mingled with; to be involved in

components.note: 厂 (a building/shelter) — 厕 relates to a structure.
则 (zé) gives a sound distantly related to 厕's reading cè, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Cèsuǒ zài nǎlǐ?
example.english: Where is the restroom?
example.fact: 厕 almost always appears in 厕所 (cèsuǒ, 'toilet, restroom'), one of the most practical everyday words to know.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 琢 originally described carving and polishing jade.
豖 gives a sound distantly related to 琢's reading zuó, having drifted apart considerably over time.

example.hanzi: 我一直在琢磨这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí zài zuómo zhège wèntí.
example.english: I've been pondering this problem.
example.fact: When read zuó (as in 琢磨, zuómo), the word means 'to ponder, mull over' — a different, colloquial reading from zhuó, which means 'to carve, polish jade,' as in 精雕细琢 (jīngdiāo xìzhuó, 'meticulous carving').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讥 relates to words spoken.
几 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 讥's reading jī, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā chángcháng jīfěng biérén.
example.english: He often mocks other people.
example.fact: 讥 means 'to mock, ridicule,' most often in 讥讽 (jīfěng, 'to satirize, taunt').

components.note: 釆 (to sort, distinguish) — the radical here; its link to 'glaze' is not obvious from the modern meaning, and 釉 borrows this shape mainly by form.
由 (yóu) gives a sound close to 釉's reading yòu, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这个花瓶上有漂亮的釉。
example.pinyin: Zhège huāpíng shàng yǒu piàoliang de yòu.
example.english: This vase has a beautiful glaze.
example.fact: 釉 names the glassy glaze coating on ceramics, giving porcelain its shiny, smooth finish.

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 窟 names a hollow space.
屈 (qū) gives a sound related to 窟's reading kū, sharing a historical root though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Dūnhuáng yǒu zhùmíng de shíkū.
example.english: Dunhuang has famous rock caves.
example.fact: 窟 names a cave or cavern, most famously in 石窟 (shíkū, 'rock-cut caves'), like the celebrated Buddhist cave art at Dunhuang.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 敛 relates to an action done to gather or hold something back.
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 敛's reading liǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他努力收敛自己的脾气。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì shōuliǎn zìjǐ de píqì.
example.english: He tries hard to restrain his temper.
example.fact: 敛 means 'to hold back, restrain,' as in 收敛 (shōuliǎn, 'to rein in, restrain oneself') — it historically also meant 'to collect (taxes, money).'

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轼 names a part of a cart.
式 (shì) gives the sound — an exact match with 轼's reading.

example.hanzi: 苏轼是中国著名的诗人。
example.pinyin: Sū Shì shì Zhōngguó zhùmíng de shīrén.
example.english: Su Shi was a famous Chinese poet.
example.fact: 轼 originally named the crossbar at the front of an ancient chariot used as an armrest; today it's best known as part of the name of the famous Song-dynasty poet 苏轼 (Sū Shì).

meanings: Mount Lu 廬山|庐山[Lu2 Shan1] in Jiangxi Province
etymologyHint: A house 广 with an open door 户; 户 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 广 (a wide, sheltering roof) — the structure of a simple building.
户 (a door) — a shelter with a door, giving 庐 its meaning 'hut, cottage.'

example.hanzi: 庐山是中国著名的风景区。
example.pinyin: Lúshān shì Zhōngguó zhùmíng de fēngjǐngqū.
example.english: Mount Lu is a famous scenic area in China.
example.fact: 庐 is a literary word for a simple hut or cottage (茅庐, máolú); it's also the name of the famous scenic mountain 庐山 (Lúshān) in Jiangxi province.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 胚 relates to a stage of biological development.
丕 (pī) gives a sound close to 胚's reading pēi, sharing the initial and differing only slightly in the vowel.

example.hanzi: 胚胎是生命最初的样子。
example.pinyin: Pēitāi shì shēngmìng zuìchū de yàngzi.
example.english: An embryo is the earliest form of life.
example.fact: 胚 means 'embryo,' as in 胚胎 (pēitāi), and by extension describes something in its earliest, unfinished stage.

meanings: (literary) to recite; to chant; to intone

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 呻 relates to a sound made with the mouth.
申 (shēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 呻's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā téng de zhí shēnyín.
example.english: He groaned continuously from the pain.
example.fact: 呻 appears in 呻吟 (shēnyín, 'to groan, moan'), describing a sound of pain or distress.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 绰 originally described something graceful and pliant, like flowing silk.
卓 (zhuó) gives a sound related to 绰's reading chuò, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Tā de chuòhào shì 'Dàlìshì'.
example.english: His nickname is 'Strongman.'
example.fact: 绰 appears in 绰号 (chuòhào, 'nickname') and 绰绰有余 (chuòchuò yǒuyú, 'more than enough, with room to spare').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扼 relates to gripping something with the hand.
厄 (è) gives the sound — an exact match with 扼's reading.

example.hanzi: 老师要求我们扼要地回答问题。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yāoqiú wǒmen èyào de huídá wèntí.
example.english: The teacher asked us to answer the question concisely.
example.fact: 扼 means 'to grip, choke,' as in 扼杀 (èshā, 'to strangle,' often used figuratively for 'to stifle') and 扼要 (èyào, 'concise, to the point').

components.note: 心 (heart) — 懿 describes an inner quality, virtue.
壹 (yī) gives a sound close to 懿's reading yì, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: '懿' 常用来形容高尚的品德。
example.pinyin: 'Yì' chángyòng lái xíngróng gāoshàng de pǐndé.
example.english: '懿' is often used to describe noble virtue.
example.fact: 懿 is a highly formal, literary word meaning 'virtuous, admirable' — historically used in honorific titles for empresses and in given names, rarely in everyday speech.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 炯 relates to brightness, like a flame.
冋 (jiōng) gives a sound close to 炯's reading jiǒng, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing jiǒngjiǒng yǒushén.
example.english: His eyes are bright and full of life.
example.fact: 炯 describes bright, piercing light, almost always in 炯炯有神 (jiǒngjiǒng yǒushén, '(eyes) bright and full of life').

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 竿 names a pole made of bamboo.
干 (gān) gives the sound — an exact match with 竿's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā ná zhe yì gēn diàoyúgān.
example.english: He's holding a fishing rod.
example.fact: 竿 names a long pole, especially of bamboo, as in 竹竿 (zhúgān, 'bamboo pole') and 钓鱼竿 (diàoyúgān, 'fishing rod').

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 慷 describes an inner quality, generosity of spirit.
康 (kāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 慷's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou hěn kāngkǎi.
example.english: He is very generous to his friends.
example.fact: 慷 appears almost only in 慷慨 (kāngkǎi, 'generous'), a common word for someone open-handed with money or help.

components.note: 虍 (tiger) — the radical here, associated with danger and vigilance.
吴 (wú) gives a sound distantly related to 虞's reading yú, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Yú shì Zhōngguó de yí gè xìngshì.
example.english: Yu is a Chinese surname.
example.fact: 虞 means 'to worry, be concerned' in classical Chinese, and is also an ancient state name and a Chinese surname today.

meanings: weight (e.g. of a steelyard or balance)

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 锤 names a metal tool.
垂 (chuí) gives the sound — an exact match with 锤's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā yòng chuízi qiāo dīngzi.
example.english: He uses a hammer to hit the nail.
example.fact: 锤 names a hammer (锤子, chuízi) and, as a verb, means 'to hammer, forge,' as in 千锤百炼 (qiānchuí bǎiliàn, 'forged through a thousand hammerings,' i.e. thoroughly tempered by experience).

components.note: 木 (wood) — 栓 originally described a wooden peg or stopper.
全 (quán) gives a sound distantly related to 栓's reading shuān, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ ménshuān chā shàng le.
example.english: He bolted the door.
example.fact: 栓 names a peg, bolt, or stopper, as in 门栓 (ménshuān, 'door bolt') and 螺栓 (luóshuān, 'a screw bolt').

components.note: 木 (wood) — 桨 names a wooden tool.
丬 gives a sound distantly related to 桨's reading jiǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā yòng jiǎng huáchuán.
example.english: He rows the boat with an oar.
example.fact: 桨 names an oar or paddle (船桨, chuánjiǎng), the wooden tool used to row a boat.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蚊 names a small flying insect.
文 (wén) gives the sound — an exact match with 蚊's reading.

example.pinyin: Xiàtiān wénzi tèbié duō.
example.english: There are especially many mosquitoes in summer.
example.fact: 蚊 names the mosquito (蚊子, wénzi), one of the most universally disliked insects, especially in summer.

meanings: used in 磅礡|磅礴[pang2 bo2]

components.note: 石 (stone) — historically, weights were made of or measured against stone.
旁 (páng) gives a sound related to 磅's reading bàng, sharing the final while the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Zhège bāoguǒ zhòng wǔ bàng.
example.english: This package weighs five pounds.
example.fact: 磅 is a phonetic loanword for the English unit 'pound,' and as a verb means 'to weigh' on a scale.

components.note: 子 (child) — 孽 originally related to offspring, especially of a concubine, later extended to 'sin, retribution.'
薛 (xuē) gives a sound distantly related to 孽's reading niè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 佛教认为做坏事会造孽。
example.pinyin: Fójiào rènwéi zuò huàishì huì zàoniè.
example.english: Buddhism holds that doing bad things creates sin.
example.fact: 孽 refers to sin or evil karma in a religious/moral sense, as in 罪孽 (zuìniè, 'sin') and 造孽 (zàoniè, 'to commit a sin').

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 惭 describes an inner feeling, shame.
斩 (zhǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 惭's reading cán, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā juéde hěn cánkuì.
example.english: He felt very ashamed.
example.fact: 惭 almost always appears in 惭愧 (cánkuì, 'ashamed, embarrassed'), describing a guilty, humbled feeling.

components.note: 戈 (a spear/weapon) — 戳 relates to poking or stabbing.
翟 (dí) gives a sound distantly related to 戳's reading chuō, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Xìnfēng shàng yǒu yí gè yóuchuō.
example.english: There's a postmark on the envelope.
example.fact: 戳 means 'to poke, stab,' and as a noun names a stamp or seal, as in 邮戳 (yóuchuō, 'postmark') and 戳子 (chuōzi, 'a stamp/seal').

meanings: to make a report (to a superior)
etymologyHint: To show 示 something to an official 亠回

components.note: 示 (to show, present) — 禀 relates to presenting information.
回, combined with the roof stroke above it, pictures an enclosed hall or office — suggesting a superior's chamber to whom a report is made, giving 禀 its meaning 'to report to a superior.'

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng shàngjí bǐngbào le qíngkuàng.
example.english: He reported the situation to his superior.
example.fact: 禀 is a formal word for 'to report to a superior,' as in 禀报 (bǐngbào) — a term rooted in old bureaucratic and imperial etiquette.

meanings: short name for Hubei 湖北[Hu2 bei3]

components.note: 阝 (a place/settlement) — 鄂 names a region.
咢 (è) gives the sound — an exact match with 鄂's reading.

example.pinyin: 'È' shì Húběi Shěng de jiǎnchēng.
example.english: "鄂" is the abbreviation for Hubei Province.
example.fact: 鄂 is the one-character abbreviation for Hubei province (湖北), commonly seen on Chinese license plates as 鄂 followed by a letter and numbers.

meanings: (literary) to make an offering to the gods
etymologyHint: Expensive 贵 food 饣; 贵 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 饣 (food) — 馈 originally related to offering food.
贵 (expensive, valuable) — a valuable offering of food, giving 馈 its meaning 'to present as a gift.'

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒmen yìxiē fǎnkuì.
example.english: Please give us some feedback.
example.fact: 馈 originally meant to present food or gifts respectfully; today it's most common in 反馈 (fǎnkuì, 'feedback'), a word used constantly in business and technology.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 垣 relates to a wall, often made of packed earth.
亘 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to 垣's reading yuán, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gǔdài chéngshì zhōuwéi yǒu chéngyuán.
example.english: Ancient cities had walls around them.
example.fact: 垣 is a literary word for a wall, especially a city or garden wall, as in 城垣 (chéngyuán, 'city wall').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 溅 relates to liquid splashing.
贱 (jiàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 溅's reading.

example.pinyin: Shuǐ jiàn dào le wǒ de yīfu shàng.
example.english: Water splashed onto my clothes.
example.fact: 溅 describes liquid splashing or spraying, as in 溅起水花 (jiàn qǐ shuǐhuā, 'to splash up water').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咚 relates to a sound being made.
冬 (dōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 咚's reading.

example.pinyin: Dōng dōng dōng, yǒurén qiāomén.
example.english: Thump thump thump, someone's knocking on the door.
example.fact: 咚 imitates a deep thumping or drumming sound, like a knock at the door or a beating drum.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — calcium is a chemical element, grouped with metals.
丐 (gài) gives the sound — an exact match with 钙's reading.

example.pinyin: Hē niúnǎi kěyǐ bǔgài.
example.english: Drinking milk can supplement calcium.
example.fact: 钙 is the chemistry term for 'calcium,' commonly discussed in the context of bone health, as in 补钙 (bǔgài, 'to take calcium supplements').

components.note: 石 (stone) — 礁 names a type of rock formation.
焦 (jiāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 礁's reading.

example.pinyin: Hǎi lǐ yǒu měilì de shānhújiāo.
example.english: There are beautiful coral reefs in the sea.
example.fact: 礁 names a reef or submerged rock, most familiar in 珊瑚礁 (shānhújiāo, 'coral reef').

components.note: 彡 (fine lines/patterns) — relates to visibility and decoration, suggesting something made evident.
章 (zhāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 彰's reading.

example.hanzi: 这件事彰显了他的勇气。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zhāngxiǎn le tā de yǒngqì.
example.english: This event demonstrated his courage.
example.fact: 彰 means 'to make evident, manifest clearly,' as in 彰显 (zhāngxiǎn) and the idiom 欲盖弥彰 (yùgài mízhāng, 'the more one tries to hide it, the more obvious it becomes').

components.note: 谷 (valley) — 豁 relates to an open gap or breach, like a valley cutting through terrain.
害 (hài) gives a sound distantly related to 豁's reading huō, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wèile mèngxiǎng, tā huō chūqù le.
example.english: For his dream, he went all out, risking everything.
example.fact: 豁 in 豁出去 (huō chūqù) means 'to go all out, risk everything without holding back' — a common colloquial expression for throwing caution to the wind.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眯 relates to an action of the eyes.
米 (mǐ) gives a sound close to 眯's reading mī, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Yángguāng tài liàng, tā mī zhe yǎnjing.
example.english: The sunlight is too bright, so he squints his eyes.
example.fact: 眯 describes narrowing the eyes, as in 眯眼 (mīyǎn, 'to squint'), and colloquially 眯一会儿 (mī yīhuìr) means 'to take a quick nap.'

components.note: 石 (mineral) — 磷 names a chemical element found in minerals.
粦 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 磷's reading.

example.hanzi: 磷是一种重要的化学元素。
example.pinyin: Lín shì yì zhǒng zhòngyào de huàxué yuánsù.
example.english: Phosphorus is an important chemical element.
example.fact: 磷 is the chemistry term for 'phosphorus,' an element essential to living cells and historically associated with the eerie glow (磷光, línguāng) sometimes seen over old graveyards at night.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 雯 relates to clouds and weather.
文 (wén) gives the sound — an exact match with 雯's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā de míngzi lǐ yǒu 'wén' zì.
example.english: Her name contains the character '雯.'
example.fact: 雯 describes colorful, patterned clouds; today it's used almost exclusively as a character in given names, especially for girls.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 墟 relates to a mound or ruined site.
虚 (xū) gives the sound — an exact match with 墟's reading.

example.hanzi: 地震后，房子变成了废墟。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn hòu, fángzi biàn chéng le fèixū.
example.english: After the earthquake, the house became ruins.
example.fact: 墟 appears in 废墟 (fèixū, 'ruins'), describing the debris left after destruction, such as from an earthquake or war.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迂 relates to a path or route.
于 (yú) gives a sound close to 迂's reading yū, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn yūhuí.
example.english: This road is very roundabout.
example.fact: 迂 describes something roundabout or impractical, as in 迂回 (yūhuí, 'circuitous') and 迂腐 (yūfǔ, 'stodgy, pedantic').

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞻 relates to looking, viewing.
詹 (zhān) gives the sound — an exact match with 瞻's reading.

example.pinyin: Rénmen qù zhānyǎng jìniànbēi.
example.english: People go to pay respects at the monument.
example.fact: 瞻 means 'to look ahead with reverence,' as in 瞻仰 (zhānyǎng, 'to view with reverence,' often said of visiting a memorial) and 前瞻 (qiánzhān, 'forward-looking').

components.note: 页 (head) — 颅 relates directly to the head.
卢 (lú) gives the sound — an exact match with 颅's reading.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de tóulú.
example.english: The doctor examined his skull.
example.fact: 颅 is a formal/medical word for the skull, as in 头颅 (tóulú, 'head, skull') and 颅骨 (lúgǔ, 'cranium').

components.note: 王 (jade) — 琉 relates to a precious, glossy material.
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — an exact match with 琉's reading.

example.hanzi: 这个花瓶是用琉璃做的。
example.pinyin: Zhège huāpíng shì yòng liúlí zuò de.
example.english: This vase is made of colored glass.
example.fact: 琉 appears in 琉璃 (liúlí, 'colored glaze, glass'), a material famous in Chinese art and traditional roof tiles (琉璃瓦).

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 悼 describes an inner feeling, grief.
卓 (zhuó) gives a sound distantly related to 悼's reading dào, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Rénmen dàoniàn shìqù de qīnrén.
example.english: People mourn their deceased relatives.
example.fact: 悼 means 'to mourn,' as in 悼念 (dàoniàn, 'to mourn, pay tribute to the dead') and 追悼会 (zhuīdàohuì, 'memorial service').

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蝴 names a type of insect.
胡 (hú) gives the sound — an exact match with 蝴's reading.

example.hanzi: 花园里有一只美丽的蝴蝶。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī měilì de húdié.
example.english: There's a beautiful butterfly in the garden.
example.fact: 蝴 exists only in 蝴蝶 (húdié, 'butterfly') — it never appears alone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拣 relates to selecting something by hand.
柬 (jiǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 拣's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā mǎi shuǐguǒ shí xǐhuan tiāojiǎn.
example.english: She likes to pick and choose when buying fruit.
example.fact: 拣 means 'to select, pick out,' as in 挑拣 (tiāojiǎn, 'to pick and choose') — closely related to and often interchangeable with 捡 (jiǎn, 'to pick up').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 渺 originally described the boundless vastness of water.
眇 (miǎo) gives the sound — an exact match with 渺's reading.

example.hanzi: 和大海比，这条船很渺小。
example.pinyin: Hé dàhǎi bǐ, zhè tiáo chuán hěn miǎoxiǎo.
example.english: Compared to the ocean, this boat is tiny.
example.fact: 渺 describes vastness or, conversely, tininess against that vastness, as in 渺小 (miǎoxiǎo, 'insignificant, tiny') and 渺茫 (miǎománg, 'dim, uncertain').

meanings: (bound form) one's family, esp. wife and children

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眷 relates to looking back fondly on something.
龹 is the historical phonetic element here; its connection to 眷's reading juàn has faded over time.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn juànliàn zìjǐ de jiāxiāng.
example.english: He feels deeply attached to his hometown.
example.fact: 眷 describes deep, caring attachment, as in 眷恋 (juànliàn, 'to be nostalgically attached to') and 家眷 (jiājuàn, 'one's family, dependents').

meanings: to sympathize; to pity; to feel compassion for
(literary) to feel sorrow; to be grieved

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 悯 describes an inner feeling, compassion.
闵 (mǐn) gives the sound — an exact match with 悯's reading.

example.hanzi: 他很怜悯那只受伤的小狗。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn liánmǐn nà zhī shòushāng de xiǎo gǒu.
example.english: He felt great pity for the injured little dog.
example.fact: 悯 almost always appears in 怜悯 (liánmǐn, 'to pity, have compassion for'), a word for feeling sympathy toward someone's suffering.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 汰 originally described washing or rinsing away.
太 (tài) gives the sound — an exact match with 汰's reading.

example.pinyin: Zhège duì bèi táotài le.
example.english: This team was eliminated.
example.fact: 汰 appears in 淘汰 (táotài, 'to eliminate, weed out'), a word used constantly for competitions, sports brackets, and evolutionary 'natural selection' (自然淘汰).

meanings: (bound form) to fear; to be cowed

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 慑 describes an inner feeling, fear.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to 慑's reading shè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 警察的出现震慑了小偷。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá de chūxiàn zhènshè le xiǎotōu.
example.english: The appearance of the police intimidated the thief.
example.fact: 慑 means 'to intimidate, overawe,' as in 震慑 (zhènshè, 'to deter through fear') and 威慑 (wēishè, 'deterrence').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 婶 names a female relative.
审 (shěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婶's reading.

example.pinyin: Wǒ shěnshen zài chúfáng zuòfàn.
example.english: My aunt is cooking in the kitchen.
example.fact: 婶 names a specific family relation: the wife of one's father's younger brother, as in 婶婶 (shěnshen) — reflecting how precisely Chinese kinship terms distinguish family roles.

components.note: 文 (culture/writing) — 斐 relates to refinement and elegance.
非 (fēi) gives a sound close to 斐's reading fěi, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì fěirán.
example.english: His achievements are remarkable.
example.fact: 斐 mainly appears in 斐然 (fěirán, 'remarkable, impressive'), as in 成绩斐然 ('remarkable achievements') — a formal, literary word.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘘 relates to a sound made with the mouth, exhaling.
虚 (xū) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘘's reading.

example.pinyin: Xū! Xiǎoshēng diǎn.
example.english: Shh! Keep your voice down.
example.fact: 嘘 is used both as an exclamation for 'shh, be quiet' and, when read as 嘘声 (xūshēng), for booing or jeering sounds of disapproval.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镶 relates to setting something into a fixed frame, often metal.
襄 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 镶's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā qù yīyuàn xiāngyá.
example.english: He went to the hospital to get a false tooth fitted.
example.fact: 镶 means 'to set, inlay,' as in 镶嵌 (xiāngqiàn, 'to inlay') and 镶牙 (xiāngyá, 'to fit a false tooth').

meanings: to dry by the heat of a fire

components.note: 火 (fire) — 炕 relates to heat, since the bed is warmed by fire underneath.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 炕's reading.

example.pinyin: Běifāng rén xǐhuan shuì kàng.
example.english: Northern Chinese people like sleeping on a heated brick bed.
example.fact: 炕 names the traditional heated brick or clay bed used in northern China, warmed from underneath by a fire, especially in winter.

etymologyHint: A minister 臣 in a statehouse 宀

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — the setting of a government building.
臣 (a minister/official) — an official within the statehouse, giving 宦 its meaning 'official, officialdom.'

example.hanzi: 古代皇宫里有很多宦官。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài huánggōng lǐ yǒu hěn duō huànguān.
example.english: There were many eunuchs in the ancient imperial palace.
example.fact: 宦 relates to serving as a government official, most familiar today in the historical term 宦官 (huànguān, 'court eunuch').

components.note: 足 (foot) — 趴 relates to the position of the body, legs splayed.
八 (bā) gives a sound close to 趴's reading pā, sharing the final though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 他累了，趴在桌子上睡着了。
example.pinyin: Tā lèi le, pā zài zhuōzi shàng shuìzháo le.
example.english: He was tired and fell asleep lying on the desk.
example.fact: 趴 means 'to lie face-down, prone,' as in the everyday phrase 趴在桌子上 (pā zài zhuōzi shàng, 'to lie face-down on the desk') — a common sight for tired students.

meanings: to draw tight; to stretch taut

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 绷 originally related to binding things tightly with thread.
朋 (péng) gives a sound distantly related to 绷's reading běng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 老师绷着脸，看起来很严肃。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī běng zhe liǎn, kàn qǐlái hěn yánsù.
example.english: The teacher kept a straight face, looking very serious.
example.fact: When read běng, 绷 describes keeping a tense, stern expression, as in 绷着脸 (běng zhe liǎn) — a different, less common reading from bēng, which means 'to stretch tight,' as in 绷带 (bēngdài, 'bandage').

components.note: 穴 (a cave/confined space) — 窘 relates to feeling cornered or trapped.
君 (jūn) gives a sound distantly related to 窘's reading jiǒng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā xiànrù le jiǒngjìng.
example.english: He fell into an awkward predicament.
example.fact: 窘 describes being caught in an awkward or difficult situation, as in 窘境 (jiǒngjìng, 'predicament') and 窘迫 (jiǒngpò, 'hard-pressed, financially strapped').

etymologyHint: Using two hands 口 to help someone remove their clothes 衣

components.note: The two 口 shapes here stand in for a pair of hands reaching in to help.
衣 (clothing) — hands helping someone with their robe, giving 襄 its meaning 'to assist, help.'

example.pinyin: Tā xiāngzhù péngyou zuò shēngyì.
example.english: He helped his friend with business.
example.fact: 襄 is a formal, literary word for 'to help, assist,' as in 襄助 (xiāngzhù) — mostly seen in set phrases like 共襄盛举 (gòngxiāng shèngjǔ, 'to jointly take part in a grand undertaking').

etymologyHint: Clear 白 jade 王; 白 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 王 (jade) — 珀 relates to a precious, gem-like material.
白 (white, clear) — a clear, translucent material, giving 珀 its meaning 'amber.'

example.hanzi: 这块琥珀里有一只小虫子。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài hǔpò lǐ yǒu yì zhī xiǎo chóngzi.
example.english: There's a little bug inside this piece of amber.
example.fact: 珀 exists almost only in 琥珀 (hǔpò, 'amber'), the fossilized tree resin prized as a gemstone — sometimes with ancient insects trapped inside.

example.pinyin: Chéngshì lǐ dàochù dōu hěn xuānxiāo.
example.english: The city is noisy and bustling everywhere.
example.fact: 嚣 describes noise and clamor, as in 喧嚣 (xuānxiāo, 'hustle and bustle, din') and 嚣张 (xiāozhāng, 'arrogant, blatantly aggressive').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拚 relates to an action carried out with intense effort.
弁 (biàn) gives a sound related to 拚's reading pàn, sharing the initial and tone though the vowel has shifted.

example.pinyin: Tā pànmìng gōngzuò zhuànqián.
example.english: He works desperately hard to earn money.
example.fact: 拚 means 'to risk everything, go all out,' as in 拚命 (pànmìng, 'to go all out, at the risk of one's life') — an alternate form of the more common 拼命.

components.note: 酉 (wine) — 酌 relates to serving or drinking wine.
勺 (sháo) gives a sound distantly related to 酌's reading zhuó, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 请你斟酌一下这个决定。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhēnzhuó yíxià zhège juédìng.
example.english: Please carefully consider this decision.
example.fact: 酌 originally meant 'to pour and drink wine'; today it mostly survives in 斟酌 (zhēnzhuó, 'to deliberate, weigh carefully') and 酌情 (zhuóqíng, 'to use discretion').

etymologyHint: A pond 氵 growing scum 虫

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浊 describes a quality of water.
虫 (a bug, scum) — water growing murky with tiny creatures and grime, giving 浊 its meaning 'muddy, turbid.'

example.pinyin: Héshuǐ biàn de hěn húnzhuó.
example.english: The river water became very muddy.
example.fact: 浊 describes muddy, turbid water or air, as in 浑浊 (húnzhuó, 'murky') — the opposite of 清 (qīng, 'clear').

meanings: (literary) to produce; to foster; to nurture

components.note: 母 (mother) — 毓 relates to bearing and raising children.

example.pinyin: 'Yù' yǒu 'yǎngyù' de yìsi.
example.english: "毓" carries the meaning of 'to nurture.'
example.fact: 毓 is a literary word meaning 'to bear and nurture children'; today it survives mainly in personal names and formal writing, rarely in everyday speech.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撼 relates to an action of shaking or moving something.
感 (gǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 撼's reading hàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这个消息震撼了所有人。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi zhènhàn le suǒyǒu rén.
example.english: This news shocked everyone.
example.fact: 撼 appears in 震撼 (zhènhàn, 'to shock, stun'), a strong word for something that deeply moves or shakes people, and 撼动 (hàndòng, 'to shake, move').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嗜 relates to eating or drinking cravings.
耆 (qí) gives a sound distantly related to 嗜's reading shì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu hē chá de shìhào.
example.english: He has a fondness for drinking tea.
example.fact: 嗜 means 'to be fond of, crave,' as in 嗜好 (shìhào, 'a strong liking, hobby') — often used for habits bordering on addiction.

meanings: to raise aloft with both hands
(of two or more people) to carry sth together
(fig.) to take on (a burden, duty etc)
etymologyHint: Labor 工 done by hand 扌; 工 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the part of the body doing the carrying.
工 (labor, work) — labor done with the hands, giving 扛 its meaning 'to carry, lift.'

example.pinyin: Tā káng zhe yí dài mǐ huí jiā.
example.english: He carried a bag of rice home on his shoulder.
