example.fact: 扛 means 'to carry on the shoulder,' as in 扛东西 (káng dōngxi); it's also read gāng in the more formal, literary sense of 'to lift with both hands,' as in 力能扛鼎 (lìnéng gāngdǐng, 'strong enough to lift a bronze cauldron').

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 峭 describes a feature of a mountain.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound close to 峭's reading qiào, sharing the final though the initial has shifted slightly.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān fēicháng dǒuqiào.
example.english: This mountain is extremely steep.
example.fact: 峭 describes steep, sheer terrain, as in 陡峭 (dǒuqiào, 'steep') and 峭壁 (qiàobì, 'a sheer cliff').

components.note: 石 (stone) — 磕 relates to knocking against something hard.
盍 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to 磕's reading kē, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn kē dào le tóu.
example.english: He accidentally bumped his head.
example.fact: 磕 means 'to knock, bump against something hard,' as in 磕到头 (kē dào tóu, 'to bump one's head') and 磕头 (kētóu, 'to kowtow').

components.note: 羽 (feathers/wings) — 翘 relates to something lifting upward, like a bird's tail feathers.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound distantly related to 翘's reading qiào, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhǐ de biānyuán qiào qǐlái le.
example.english: The edge of the paper curled up.
example.fact: 翘 describes something curling or tilting upward, as in a warped page (翘起来, qiào qǐlái) — read qiáo, the same character also means 'to look up expectantly,' as in 翘首 (qiáoshǒu).

components.note: 木 (wood) — 槽 originally described a wooden trough.
曹 (cáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 槽's reading.

example.pinyin: Shuǐcáo lǐ yǒu hěn duō zāng wǎn.
example.english: There are many dirty bowls in the sink.
example.fact: 槽 names a trough or basin, as in 水槽 (shuǐcáo, 'sink'); in internet slang, it also appears in 吐槽 (tùcáo, 'to poke fun at, complain about'), borrowed from Japanese.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淌 relates to flowing liquid.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to 淌's reading tǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Héshuǐ jìngjìng de liútǎng.
example.english: The river water flows quietly.
example.fact: 淌 describes liquid flowing or trickling, as in 流淌 (liútǎng, 'to flow') — often said of rivers, tears, or sweat.

etymologyHint: A fence 册 made of wood 木; 册 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 木 (wood) — fences are traditionally made of wood.
册 depicts a bound stack of slats — like the boards of a fence lined up side by side, giving 栅 its meaning 'fence, palisade.'

example.pinyin: Huāyuán zhōuwéi yǒu yì quān zhàlan.
example.english: There's a fence around the garden.
example.fact: 栅 almost always appears in 栅栏 (zhàlan, 'fence, railing'), a common word for a barrier made of wood or metal bars.

etymologyHint: A bald 秃 head 页; 秃 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 秃 (bald) — a head that has lost its hair.
页 (head) — combined with 'bald,' the image of a head worn down or in decline, giving 颓 its meaning 'ruined, decayed, dispirited.'

example.pinyin: Tā shīyè hòu biàn de hěn tuífèi.
example.english: After losing his job, he became very listless and dispirited.
example.fact: 颓 describes decline or dispiritedness, as in 颓废 (tuífèi, 'decadent, listless') and 衰颓 (shuāituí, 'to decline, deteriorate').

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 熏 relates to smoke and fumes rising from fire.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì xūnròu, hěn hǎochī.
example.english: This is smoked meat; it's delicious.
example.fact: 熏 means 'to smoke, fumigate with fumes,' as in 熏肉 (xūnròu, 'smoked meat') and 熏香 (xūnxiāng, 'to burn incense').

components.note: 王 (jade) — 瑛 describes the luster of jade or crystal.
英 (yīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 瑛's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā de míngzi lǐ yǒu 'yīng' zì.
example.english: Her name contains the character '瑛.'
example.fact: 瑛 is a literary word for the sparkle of fine jade or crystal; today it's used almost exclusively as a character in given names.

components.note: 页 (head) — 颐 relates to a part of the head, the jaw and cheek.
臣 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to 颐's reading yí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 颐和园是北京著名的皇家园林。
example.pinyin: Yíhéyuán shì Běijīng zhùmíng de huángjiā yuánlín.
example.english: The Summer Palace is a famous imperial garden in Beijing.
example.fact: 颐 originally meant the jaw or cheek, and by extension 'to nourish, rest.' It's most familiar today as part of 颐和园 (Yíhéyuán, 'the Summer Palace'), the famous imperial garden in Beijing.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 忖 relates to an act of thinking.
寸 (cùn) gives a sound close to 忖's reading cǔn, sharing the base syllable and differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā xīnlǐ sīcǔn le hěn jiǔ.
example.english: He pondered in his heart for a long time.
example.fact: 忖 means 'to ponder, guess,' as in 思忖 (sīcǔn, 'to ponder') and 忖度 (cǔnduó, 'to speculate about').
